limits.text: No PDF/UA check was run on the worksheet PDFs.
No keyboard-only or screen-reader pass was made.
No planner or finance officer reviewed whether the worksheets are useful. Agent-run checks are the acceptance evidence.
The worksheets are not payment requests and no request was sent to a funder. A recipient requests payment on the form its funder requires; no SF-270, SF-271 or LAPM Exhibit 5-A was made.
Nothing in this record or the worksheets states that any cost is allowable, eligible or reimbursable, or that any balance was deobligated.
This record and the worksheets are not an accounting record or an audit trail, and no agency may rely on them for a single audit.

The award, its amounts and its requests are demonstration figures typed by an automated proof run under a demonstration label. No real award was made, and no agency, tribe, funder or program officer took part.
Paid, and each payment date, is what the workspace typed. No funder confirmed a payment.
No funder reference, such as a voucher or payment number, is recorded for any request.

No retention was entered. A reconciled close-out today releases the ceiling minus net paid, which would count retention the funder holds as released (KI-2026-11-17-031), so the proof does not exercise retention.

Each journey leaves its accounts, workspace, project, tracked opportunity, award, requests and close-out on the hosted site under the demonstration label, with one unlinked draft request from the refused claim above the ceiling. It publishes nothing and opens no public page.

The journey read or set these and the checker cannot read them again: each status the routes answered and the control that sent it, every time, the screen readings, the profile each request carried, the statuses the owner, the member and the second account received, the database's answers to each direct write, the accessibility results, console errors and sideways scroll of each screen, how the account was confirmed, the executor, and which build, mode and harness checkout ran.
